annotations: Starting, steering, watching and answering a session

Transcripts for the four session commands. Each block is drawn at a fixed column width. The dashed line marks the last column, and each header reports the longest line so the test is visible. Amber appears only while a gate is waiting on a person.
Every string these transcripts introduce, grouped by the command that prints it. Angle brackets are values filled in at runtime.

Desktop V2 labels its step 3 gate "Hard gate" yet offers "Always for prisma migrate here". Under the rule in this brief, a hard gate never offers it. I drew prisma migrate as an ordinary gate and used a delete outside the project as the hard gate. Which classification is right, and which surface changes?
Can a person choose Always here outside watch? The approve command has no way to say it. I left it interactive only rather than invent a flag.

A script calling approve on a hard gate is refused with 33, so a script can never be the person. Deny works from anywhere. Is a terminal attached to stdin enough proof of a person, or does a hard gate need a device credential with a decide scope as well?
When does send land: when the current tool call returns (drawn), or at the next turn boundary like a model change?
Does watch exit when the turn ends (drawn), or keep following later turns?
Reconnect attempts and backoff are not specified anywhere. I drew five attempts, doubling from 2s. The daemon side is also open: how long does it keep a result for a client that has not come back?
The receipt line "checkpoint ckpt_7f24 taken before it ran" depends on the per-approval checkpoint, which Desktop V2 marks as proposed. Drop the line until it ships?
Both layouts use · − … and B uses box drawing characters. What does the CLI print when the locale is not UTF-8, and is NO_COLOR honoured? Layout A survives both because every state is also a word.
The policy refusal says only an org owner can change the rule. Should it also name where, and does a solo account have an owner?
The exit code numbers are proposed. Which are frozen for 1.0, and is 130 right for Ctrl-C when the session keeps running?

humanRead.note: Built for Q391 A: the whole table, adopted before 1.0, in apps/cli/src/exit-codes.ts, printed by --help and used by every exit. Daemon unreachable moved from 1 to 3; an unpaired client moved from usage (2) to a named code the design does not draw, not-paired (5), placed with the other nothing-was-sent codes (a substitution recorded under Q389). The row for 1 drops the design's clause that a log path is printed, because the CLI keeps no log. Codes 4 and 10 to 130 are reserved for the session commands, which cli.session-commands still lists as missing. A failed doctor probe, a declined or refused skill install and a pairing the daemon refused have no row in the design and exit 1 for M1 (Q423 A, 2026-10-03).

Built for Q394 A as a renderer in apps/cli/src/transcript.ts; no command prints it yet (cli.session-commands is missing). Facts come one per line from the approval on the wire: machine, working dir, affects, network, estimated. The design's machine fact also names the transport (mac-mini-m4 · loopback); the approval carries the machine only, so the transport is not drawn. The step line prints step n of m or asked by the agent, not in the plan only when the caller knows which; otherwise agent · mode alone, because the approval does not say. A tool-server call offers Allow once and Deny only (ruled 2026-09-26), which the design does not draw. So does a gate whose command the daemon could not resolve (execution.state unresolved): the daemon refuses a standing rule for it (ruled 2026-09-24) and the web and desktop cards hide the button; the design does not draw that case either.

Built for Q392 A: the person is the paired device's label, then the client kind and machine, as in allowed once by dana · cli on mac-mini-m4 · 14:07:11. The receipt thread item now carries the paired device the daemon verified (Q424 A), so the renderer takes the label from the receipt's device, label before client kind as the web and desktop receipt reads, whichever client decided. A receipt without a device (the daemon credential, or a row written before the field) takes a label from the caller, and with none names the client kind alone, as allowed once by desktop on mac-mini-m4 · 14:07:11, which the design does not draw. The design's checkpoint line is not drawn, as its own open question proposes, and an Always decision has no line in the design so it has none here.

Built for Q393 A: set by and applies to print what the daemon put in setBy and scope, which in M1 are the permission mode and the session; the design's org-owner values and its closing note about an org owner are not drawn. The override line keeps the design's constant, none, not even with approval, which the daemon enforces by refusing before the command runs. The body is the operation sentence the daemon sends, printed after the command.
Q392 A: M1 has no accounts, so the <person> in receipts and watch lines (allowed once by dana) is the device label and client kind.

Both fit 80 columns. Set the columns tweak to 72 or 60 to see the difference: A only loses right-aligned meta, while B's border wraps into noise. A also stays greppable in a CI log and keeps its meaning without colour, because every state is a word. B reads as a stronger interrupt, which the amber header line already gives A.

The client lost the daemon, not the work. A call in flight shows as unconfirmed until the daemon says otherwise. On reconnect watch replays what the daemon recorded. If the daemon has no result either, the turn stops rather than guessing.
